purpose: Move managed release-pull-request policy from the GitHub composite-action shell script into a typed, provider-neutral Callisto decision boundary.
scope: The credential-free observation, deterministic decision, CLI JSON interface, GitHub snapshot collector, thin GitHub executor, and black-box contract tests for creating, updating, superseding, and retaining a Callisto-managed release PR.
non_goals: Making a GitHub pull request or its metadata release authority after merge.
Putting forge tokens, raw credentials, shell commands, or arbitrary GitHub API responses in durable release intent/state/receipt records.
Changing the merged-release-commit authority, artifact, or execute contracts from SPEC-RELEASE-INTERFACES-013.

architecture.observation: The action gathers a small, credential-free snapshot of the configured repository's open managed PRs and branch workflow-delta facts. Callisto validates that snapshot against explicit configured base/release branch identity; it never accepts caller-side preselection of an existing PR.
architecture.decision: Callisto determines whether pending changesets require no PR, a new canonical PR, an update of exactly one canonical or SHA-suffixed managed PR, or a replacement PR. The decision names exact expected PR number/branch facts so the executor can detect a race before mutation.
architecture.execution: The composite action invokes `callisto release-pr decide`, then only executes the returned operation: version from the current base, commit/push the selected branch, create or edit the named PR, and when required close only the named superseded PR with the returned replacement URL. It may render a body, manage a configured label, and re-observe expected state, but it does not independently choose an operation or branch.
architecture.authority: This is pre-merge collaboration policy, not durable release authority. After merge, SPEC-RELEASE-EXECUTION-FOUNDATION-007's parent-to-commit validation remains the sole release authority.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: `callisto release-pr decide` accepts an explicit versioned snapshot and explicit configured base/release branch identity, computes whether the workspace has pending changesets, and emits a versioned JSON decision. It is read-only and does not invoke GitHub, push, write manifests, create a PR, tag, publish, or acquire ApplyPermit.

The decision model accepts only PRs from the configured repository whose head is either the exact canonical managed branch or its exact lower-case forty-hex SHA-suffixed replacement. Zero eligible PRs yields create; exactly one yields update unless its observed workflow delta requires supersede; more than one fails closed. Lookalike prefixes, foreign repositories, malformed suffixes, a mismatched base branch, duplicate numbers, or unsupported schema versions fail before any mutation.

A supersede decision deterministically names the SHA-suffixed replacement branch from the current base commit, the exact old PR number, and the expected old branch. An ordinary later run retains that replacement branch. A no-pending-changesets decision is a no-op and the executor performs no Git or GitHub mutation.

The GitHub action is a thin executor of the Callisto decision: it gathers the snapshot without caller-controlled jq filtering, calls the CLI, branches only on the closed decision kind, and rechecks the decision's expected PR/branch facts immediately before each forge mutation. Tests execute the exact script with recording Git/GitHub boundaries and demonstrate create, update, supersede, retained replacement, no-op, ambiguity, foreign/lookalike rejection, and stale-observation refusal.

The CLI model and action outputs are credential-free, schema-versioned, and stable for machine consumption. Diagnostics use typed miette errors on invalid snapshots; user-supplied PR body content is not persisted in the decision and remains body-rendering input only.

revision_note: Extracted from SPEC-RELEASE-INTERFACES-013 after review identified that the existing Bash action was rediscovering create/update/supersede policy. This spec narrows the change to pre-merge release-PR collaboration while preserving the already specified post-merge durable authority boundary.
